sanskrit: te dahyamānāḥ pārthena pāvakeneva kuñjarāḥ samāsīdanta kauravyā vadhyamānāḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Scorched by Pārtha as elephants are scorched by fire, the Kauravas, struck down by his whetted arrows, sank to the ground.

sanskrit: śaracāpadharaḥ pārthaḥ prajvalann iva bhārata dadāha samare yodhān kakṣam agnir iva jvalan
english: Bearing his bow and arrows, Pārtha, blazing as it were, O Bhārata, burned up the warriors in battle as a flaming fire consumes dry brushwood.

sanskrit: yathā vanānte vanapair visṛṣṭaḥ; kakṣaṃ dahet kṛṣṇagatiḥ saghoṣaḥ bhūridrumaṃ śuṣkalatāvitānaṃ; bhṛśaṃ samṛddho jvalanaḥ pratāpī
english: As at the forest's edge a roaring blaze, set loose by the woodsmen and leaving a black trail, would burn the thicket thick with trees and canopied with withered creepers—a fierce conflagration grown mightily in strength—

sanskrit: evaṃ sa nārācagaṇapratāpī; śarārcir uccāvacatigmatejāḥ dadāha sarvāṃ tava putrasenām; amṛṣyamāṇas tarasā tarasvī
english: even so did he, blazing with his volleys of iron shafts, his arrows for flames and his fierce radiance flaring high and low, in his impetuous fury, brooking nothing, the swift one, burn up the whole army of your sons.

sanskrit: tasyeṣavaḥ prāṇaharāḥ sumuktā; nāsajjan vai varmasu rukmapuṅkhāḥ na ca dvitīyaṃ pramumoca bāṇaṃ; nare haye vā paramadvipe vā
english: His life-taking arrows, well loosed and golden-feathered, were not stayed by any armor; nor did he loose a second shaft upon a man, a horse, or a mighty elephant.

sanskrit: anekarūpākṛtibhir hi bāṇair; mahārathānīkam anupraviśya sa eva ekas tava putrasenāṃ; jaghāna daityān iva vajrapāṇiḥ
english: For with arrows of many shapes and forms he penetrated the host of great chariot-warriors, and he alone slew the army of your sons as the Wielder of the Thunderbolt slew the Daityas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca asyatāṃ yatamānānāṃ śūrāṇām anivartinām saṃkalpam akaron moghaṃ gāṇḍīvena dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Of those heroes who hurled their weapons and strove and would not turn back, Dhanaṃjaya with the Gāṇḍīva made every resolve come to nothing.

sanskrit: indrāśanisamasparśān aviṣahyān mahaujasaḥ visṛjan dṛśyate bāṇān dhārā muñcann ivāmbudaḥ
english: He was seen loosing arrows whose touch was like Indra's thunderbolt, unbearable and of vast power, as a thundercloud pours down its torrents.

sanskrit: tat sainyaṃ bharataśreṣṭha vadhyamānaṃ kirīṭinā saṃpradudrāva saṃgrāmāt tava putrasya paśyataḥ
english: That army, O best of the Bhāratas, being slaughtered by the Diademed One, fled from the battle before the very eyes of your son.

sanskrit: hatadhuryā rathāḥ ke cid dhatasūtās tathāpare bhagnākṣayugacakreṣāḥ ke cid āsan viśāṃ pate
english: Some chariots had their draught-horses slain, others their charioteers killed, and some, O lord of peoples, had their axles, yokes, wheels, and poles shattered.

sanskrit: anyeṣāṃ sāyakāḥ kṣīṇās tathānye śarapīḍitāḥ akṣatā yugapat ke cit prādravan bhayapīḍitāḥ
english: Others had their arrows spent, and others were tormented by shafts; and some, though unwounded, fled all together, oppressed by fear.

sanskrit: ke cit putrān upādāya hatabhūyiṣṭhavāhanāḥ vicukruśuḥ pitṝn anye sahāyān apare punaḥ
english: Some, taking up their sons, their mounts for the most part slain, cried aloud; others called upon their fathers, and yet others upon their comrades.

sanskrit: bāndhavāṃś ca naravyāghra bhrātṝn saṃbandhinas tathā dudruvuḥ ke cid utsṛjya tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: And some, O tiger among men, abandoning their kinsmen, their brothers and their relations here and there, took to flight, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: bahavo 'tra bhṛśaṃ viddhā muhyamānā mahārathāḥ niṣṭanantaḥ sma dṛśyante pārthabāṇahatā narāḥ
english: Many great chariot-warriors there, grievously pierced and swooning, were seen groaning—men struck down by Pārtha's arrows.

sanskrit: tān anye ratham āropya samāśvāsya muhūrtakam viśrāntāś ca vitṛṣṇāś ca punar yuddhāya jagmire
english: Others, mounting them upon a chariot and reviving them for a while, once rested and their thirst quenched, went again to the fight.

sanskrit: tān apāsya gatāḥ ke cit punar eva yuyutsavaḥ kurvantas tava putrasya śāsanaṃ yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: Some, having set them aside and gone, returned once more eager to fight, frenzied for battle, carrying out the command of your son.

sanskrit: pānīyam apare pītvā paryāśvāsya ca vāhanam varmāṇi ca samāropya ke cid bharatasattama
english: Others, having drunk water and refreshed their mounts and donned their armor again, O best of the Bhāratas—

sanskrit: samāśvāsyāpare bhrātṝn nikṣipya śibire 'pi ca putrān anye pitṝn anye punar yuddham arocayan
english: and others, having revived their brothers and set them down in the camp—some their sons and some their fathers—once more longed for battle.

sanskrit: sajjayitvā rathān ke cid yathāmukhyaṃ viśāṃ pate āplutya pāṇḍavānīkaṃ punar yuddham arocayan
english: Some, having made ready their chariots each in due order, O lord of peoples, and charging upon the Pāṇḍava host, once more longed for battle.

sanskrit: te śūrāḥ kiṅkiṇījālaiḥ samācchannā babhāsire trailokyavijaye yuktā yathā daiteyadānavāḥ
english: Those heroes, covered over with nets of little bells, shone forth like the Daityas and Dānavas bent upon the conquest of the three worlds.

sanskrit: āgamya sahasā ke cid rathaiḥ svarṇavibhūṣitaiḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkeṣu dhṛṣṭadyumnam ayodhayan
english: Some, coming on suddenly in chariots adorned with gold, fought against Dhṛṣṭadyumna amid the ranks of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi pāñcālyaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ nākuliś ca śatānīko rathānīkam ayodhayan
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna the Pāñcāla, and Śikhaṇḍin the great chariot-warrior, and Śatānīka the son of Nakula did battle against that host of chariots.

sanskrit: pāñcālyas tu tataḥ kruddhaḥ sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ abhyadravat susaṃrabdhas tāvakān hantum udyataḥ
english: Then the Pāñcāla, enraged and surrounded by a great force, charged in fury, eager to slay your men.

sanskrit: tatas tv āpatatas tasya tava putro janādhipa bāṇasaṃghān anekān vai preṣayām āsa bhārata
english: Then, as he rushed on, your son, O ruler of men, sent forth against him many a volley of arrows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tato rājaṃs tava putreṇa dhanvinā nārācair bahubhiḥ kṣipraṃ bāhvor urasi cārpitaḥ
english: Then, O king, Dhṛṣṭadyumna was swiftly struck in the arms and the breast by your son the archer with many iron shafts.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsas tottrārdita iva dvipaḥ tasyāśvāṃś caturo bāṇaiḥ preṣayām āsa mṛtyave sāratheś cāsya bhallena śiraḥ kāyād apāharat
english: That mighty archer, deeply pierced like an elephant goaded by the hook, sent his four horses to their death with his arrows, and with a broad-headed shaft swept the head of his charioteer from its body.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā pṛṣṭham āruhya vājinaḥ apākrāmad dhataratho nātidūram ariṃdamaḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana, his chariot destroyed, mounted upon the back of a horse and withdrew a little way, that subduer of foes.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu hatavikrāntaṃ svam anīkaṃ mahābalaḥ tava putro mahārāja prayayau yatra saubalaḥ
english: But seeing his own host broken in prowess, your mighty son, O great king, went to where the son of Subala was.

sanskrit: tato ratheṣu bhagneṣu trisāhasrā mahādvipāḥ pāṇḍavān rathinaḥ pañca samantāt paryavārayan
english: Then, when the chariots were broken, three thousand great elephants surrounded on every side the five Pāṇḍava chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: te vṛtāḥ samare pañca gajānīkena bhārata aśobhanta naravyāghrā grahā vyāptā ghanair iva
english: Those five, encircled in battle by the host of elephants, O Bhārata, those tigers among men shone like planets veiled in clouds.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno mahārāja labdhalakṣo mahābhujaḥ viniryayau rathenaiva śvetāśvaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ
english: Then Arjuna, O great king, the mighty-armed, a sure marksman, with his white horses and Kṛṣṇa for his charioteer, sallied forth in his chariot.

sanskrit: taiḥ samantāt parivṛtaḥ kuñjaraiḥ parvatopamaiḥ nārācair vimalais tīkṣṇair gajānīkam apothayat
english: Surrounded on all sides by those elephants like mountains, he crushed that host of elephants with his bright, sharp iron shafts.

sanskrit: tatraikabāṇanihatān apaśyāma mahāgajān patitān pātyamānāṃś ca vibhinnān savyasācinā
english: There we saw great elephants slain each by a single arrow, fallen and falling and torn asunder by Savyasācin.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu tān dṛṣṭvā nāgān mattagajopamaḥ kareṇa gṛhya mahatīṃ gadām abhyapatad balī avaplutya rathāt tūrṇaṃ daṇḍapāṇir ivāntakaḥ
english: But Bhīmasena, beholding those elephants—he, the mighty one, like a maddened elephant himself—seized his great mace in his hand and, leaping swiftly down from his chariot, fell upon them like Death with his rod in hand.

sanskrit: tam udyatagadaṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahāratham vitresus tāvakāḥ sainyāḥ śakṛnmūtraṃ prasusruvuḥ āvignaṃ ca balaṃ sarvaṃ gadāhaste vṛkodare
english: Seeing that great chariot-warrior of the Pāṇḍavas with his mace upraised, your soldiers trembled and voided their dung and urine; and the whole host was thrown into terror when Vṛkodara held his mace in hand.

sanskrit: gadayā bhīmasenena bhinnakumbhān rajasvalān dhāvamānān apaśyāma kuñjarān parvatopamān
english: We saw elephants like mountains, their frontal globes split by Bhīmasena's mace, covered with dust and running wildly.

sanskrit: pradhāvya kuñjarās te tu bhīmasenagadāhatāḥ petur ārtasvaraṃ kṛtvā chinnapakṣā ivādrayaḥ
english: Those elephants, having charged forth and been struck by Bhīmasena's mace, fell with a cry of anguish like mountains whose wings had been clipped.

sanskrit: tān bhinnakumbhān subahūn dravamāṇān itas tataḥ patamānāṃś ca saṃprekṣya vitresus tava sainikāḥ
english: Beholding those many elephants with their temples split, fleeing this way and that and falling, your soldiers were seized with terror.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro 'pi saṃkruddho mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau gṛdhrapakṣaiḥ śitair bāṇair jaghnur vai gajayodhinaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira too, in great wrath, and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī slew the elephant-fighters with their whetted, vulture-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu samare parājitya narādhipam apakrānte tava sute hayapṛṣṭhaṃ samāśrite
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna, having vanquished the king in battle—when your son had withdrawn and taken refuge upon the back of a horse—

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca pāṇḍavān sarvān kuñjaraiḥ parivāritān dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārāja saha sarvaiḥ prabhadrakaiḥ putraḥ pāñcālarājasya jighāṃsuḥ kuñjarān yayau
english: and seeing all the Pāṇḍavas surrounded by the elephants, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, the son of the Pāñcāla king, together with all the Prabhadrakas, went forth eager to slay those elephants.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭvā tu rathānīke duryodhanam ariṃdamam aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ apṛcchan kṣatriyāṃs tatra kva nu duryodhano gataḥ
english: But not seeing Duryodhana the subduer of foes among the host of chariots, Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman the Sātvata asked the warriors there: "Where now has Duryodhana gone?"

sanskrit: apaśyamānā rājānaṃ vartamāne janakṣaye manvānā nihataṃ tatra tava putraṃ mahārathāḥ viṣaṇṇavadanā bhūtvā paryapṛcchanta te sutam
english: Not seeing the king while the slaughter of men went on, those great chariot-warriors, thinking your son slain there, with downcast faces asked after your son.

sanskrit: āhuḥ ke cid dhate sūte prayāto yatra saubalaḥ apare tv abruvaṃs tatra kṣatriyā bhṛśavikṣatāḥ
english: Some said, "His charioteer being slain, he has gone where the son of Subala is"; but others among the sorely wounded warriors said otherwise.

sanskrit: duryodhanena kiṃ kāryaṃ drakṣyadhvaṃ yadi jīvati yudhyadhvaṃ sahitāḥ sarve kiṃ vo rājā kariṣyati
english: "What need have you of Duryodhana? You shall see him if he lives. Fight, all of you together! What will the king do for you?"

sanskrit: te kṣatriyāḥ kṣatair gātrair hatabhūyiṣṭhavāhanāḥ śaraiḥ saṃpīḍyamānāś ca nātivyaktam ivābruvan
english: Those warriors, their limbs wounded and their mounts for the most part slain, and themselves tormented by arrows, spoke as it were indistinctly.

sanskrit: idaṃ sarvaṃ balaṃ hanmo yena sma parivāritāḥ ete sarve gajān hatvā upayānti sma pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "Let us slay this whole force by which we have been surrounded. These Pāṇḍavas, having slain our elephants, are all advancing upon us."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣām aśvatthāmā mahābalaḥ hitvā pāñcālarājasya tad anīkaṃ durutsaham
english: But hearing their words, the mighty Aśvatthāman, leaving behind that irresistible host of the Pāñcāla king—

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca prayayur yatra saubalaḥ rathānīkaṃ parityajya śūrāḥ sudṛḍhadhanvinaḥ
english: and Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman—those heroes of the firmest bows, abandoning the host of chariots, went to where the son of Subala was.

sanskrit: tatas teṣu prayāteṣu dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ āyayuḥ pāṇḍavā rājan vinighnantaḥ sma tāvakān
english: Then, when they had gone, the Pāṇḍavas, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head, came on, O king, slaughtering your men.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu tān āpatataḥ saṃprahṛṣṭān mahārathān parākrāntāṃs tato vīrān nirāśāñ jīvite tadā vivarṇamukhabhūyiṣṭham abhavat tāvakaṃ balam
english: Seeing those great chariot-warriors rushing on, exultant and bold, those heroes who had then given up all hope of life, your host became for the most part pale of face.

sanskrit: parikṣīṇāyudhān dṛṣṭvā tān ahaṃ parivāritān rājan balena dvyaṅgena tyaktvā jīvitam ātmanaḥ
english: Seeing them surrounded, their weapons spent, I, O king, with a force of two divisions, having staked my own life—

sanskrit: ātmanāpañcamo 'yudhyaṃ pāñcālasya balena ha tasmin deśe vyavasthāpya yatra śāradvataḥ sthitaḥ
english: myself the fifth, fought against the host of the Pāñcāla, taking my stand in that place where the son of Śaradvat stood.

sanskrit: saṃprayuddhā vayaṃ pañca kirīṭiśarapīḍitāḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ mahānīkaṃ tatra no 'bhūd raṇo mahān jitās tena vayaṃ sarve vyapayāma raṇāt tataḥ
english: We five joined battle, tormented by the arrows of the Diademed One, against Dhṛṣṭadyumna and his great host; there was a mighty struggle there for us. Vanquished by him, we all withdrew thereupon from the fight.

sanskrit: athāpaśyaṃ sātyakiṃ tam upāyāntaṃ mahāratham rathaiś catuḥśatair vīro māṃ cābhyadravad āhave
english: Then I saw Sātyaki, that great chariot-warrior, coming on with four hundred chariots, and the hero charged at me in the battle.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnād ahaṃ muktaḥ kathaṃ cic chrāntavāhanaḥ patito mādhavānīkaṃ duṣkṛtī narakaṃ yathā tatra yuddham abhūd ghoraṃ muhūrtam atidāruṇam
english: Hardly escaped from Dhṛṣṭadyumna, my mounts wearied, I fell upon the host of the Mādhava as an evildoer falls into hell. There the battle was dreadful for a while, exceedingly terrible.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu mahābāhur mama hatvā paricchadam jīvagrāham agṛhṇān māṃ mūrchitaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi
english: But the mighty-armed Sātyaki, having slain my retinue, took me captive alive as I lay swooning, fallen upon the ground.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād iva tad gajānīkam avadhyata gadayā bhīmasenena nārācair arjunena ca
english: Then in but a moment that host of elephants was destroyed—by the mace of Bhīmasena and by the iron shafts of Arjuna.

sanskrit: pratipiṣṭair mahānāgaiḥ samantāt parvatopamaiḥ nātiprasiddheva gatiḥ pāṇḍavānām ajāyata
english: With the great elephants like mountains crushed all around, the passage of the Pāṇḍavas became, as it were, not easily made.

sanskrit: rathamārgāṃs tataś cakre bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārāja vyapakarṣan mahāgajān
english: Then the mighty Bhīmasena cleared paths for the chariots of the Pāṇḍavas, O great king, by dragging away the great elephants.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ apaśyanto rathānīke duryodhanam ariṃdamam rājānaṃ mṛgayām āsus tava putraṃ mahāratham
english: Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman the Sātvata, not seeing Duryodhana the subduer of foes among the host of chariots, went searching for the king, your son, that great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: parityajya ca pāñcālaṃ prayātā yatra saubalaḥ rājño 'darśanasaṃvignā vartamāne janakṣaye
english: And leaving the Pāñcāla behind, they went to where the son of Subala was, distraught at not seeing the king while the slaughter of men went on.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca gajānīke hate tasmin pāṇḍuputreṇa bhārata vadhyamāne bale caiva bhīmasenena saṃyuge
english: Saṃjaya said: When that host of elephants had been destroyed by the son of Pāṇḍu, O Bhārata, and the army was being slaughtered by Bhīmasena in the battle,

sanskrit: carantaṃ ca tathā dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenam ariṃdamam daṇḍahastaṃ yathā kruddham antakaṃ prāṇahāriṇam
english: and seeing Bhīmasena the subduer of foes ranging thus, like wrathful, life-taking Death with his rod in hand—

sanskrit: sametya samare rājan hataśeṣāḥ sutās tava adṛśyamāne kauravye putre duryodhane tava sodaryāḥ sahitā bhūtvā bhīmasenam upādravan
english: the surviving sons of yours, O king, gathering together in the battle—since the Kaurava, your son Duryodhana, was nowhere to be seen—those brothers of one womb, joining as one, rushed upon Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: durmarṣaṇo mahārāja jaitro bhūribalo raviḥ ity ete sahitā bhūtvā tava putrāḥ samantataḥ bhīmasenam abhidrutya rurudhuḥ sarvatodiśam
english: Durmarṣaṇa, O great king, Jaitra, Bhūribala, and Ravi—these your sons, joining as one, charged upon Bhīmasena from every side and hemmed him in on all quarters.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahārāja svarathaṃ punar āsthitaḥ mumoca niśitān bāṇān putrāṇāṃ tava marmasu
english: Then Bhīma, O great king, mounting once more upon his own chariot, loosed whetted arrows into the vital parts of your sons.

sanskrit: te kīryamāṇā bhīmena putrās tava mahāraṇe bhīmasenam apāsedhan pravaṇād iva kuñjaram
english: Your sons, overwhelmed by Bhīma in that great battle, sought to drive Bhīmasena back as one might turn an elephant back from a slope.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho raṇe bhīmaḥ śiro durmarṣaṇasya ha kṣurapreṇa pramathyāśu pātayām āsa bhūtale
english: Then Bhīma, enraged in the fight, swiftly struck off the head of Durmarṣaṇa with a razor-edged arrow and brought it down to the ground.

sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa bhallena sarvāvaraṇabhedinā śrutāntam avadhīd bhīmas tava putraṃ mahārathaḥ
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft that pierced through every armor, Bhīma the great chariot-warrior slew your son Śrutānta.

sanskrit: jayatsenaṃ tato viddhvā nārācena hasann iva pātayām āsa kauravyaṃ rathopasthād ariṃdamaḥ sa papāta rathād rājan bhūmau tūrṇaṃ mamāra ca
english: Then, piercing Jayatsena with an iron shaft as if in mirth, the subduer of foes felled that Kaurava from the floor of his chariot; and he fell from the car, O king, to the earth, and swiftly died.

sanskrit: śrutarvā tu tato bhīmaṃ kruddho vivyādha māriṣa śatena gṛdhravājānāṃ śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām
english: Then Śrutarvan, in wrath, pierced Bhīma, O honored one, with a hundred straight-jointed arrows fledged with vulture feathers.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho raṇe bhīmo jaitraṃ bhūribalaṃ ravim trīn etāṃs tribhir ānarchad viṣāgnipratimaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Bhīma, enraged in the fight, struck these three—Jaitra, Bhūribala, and Ravi—with three arrows like poison and fire.

sanskrit: te hatā nyapatan bhūmau syandanebhyo mahārathāḥ vasante puṣpaśabalā nikṛttā iva kiṃśukāḥ
english: Those great chariot-warriors, slain, fell from their chariots to the ground like kiṃśuka trees in springtime, dappled with blossoms, cut down.

sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa tīkṣṇena nārācena paraṃtapaḥ durvimocanam āhatya preṣayām āsa mṛtyave
english: Then that scorcher of foes, striking Durvimocana with another sharp iron shaft, sent him to his death.

sanskrit: sa hataḥ prāpatad bhūmau svarathād rathināṃ varaḥ gires tu kūṭajo bhagno māruteneva pādapaḥ
english: Slain, that foremost of chariot-warriors fell to the ground from his own car, like a tree growing on a mountain peak broken by the wind.

sanskrit: duṣpradharṣaṃ tataś caiva sujātaṃ ca sutau tava ekaikaṃ nyavadhīt saṃkhye dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ camūmukhe tau śilīmukhaviddhāṅgau petatū rathasattamau
english: Then he slew Duṣpradharṣa and Sujāta, two of your sons, each with two arrows apiece in the battle, at the head of the host; and those two foremost of chariot-warriors fell, their limbs pierced by his shafts.

sanskrit: tato yatantam aparam abhivīkṣya sutaṃ tava bhallena yudhi vivyādha bhīmo durviṣahaṃ raṇe sa papāta hato vāhāt paśyatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: Then, marking another of your sons striving in the fight, Bhīma, hard to withstand in battle, pierced him with a broad-headed shaft; and he fell slain from his mount before the eyes of all the archers.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu nihatān bhrātṝn bahūn ekena saṃyuge amarṣavaśam āpannaḥ śrutarvā bhīmam abhyayāt
english: But seeing his many brothers slain by one man in the battle, Śrutarvan, overcome with indignation, advanced upon Bhīma.

sanskrit: vikṣipan sumahac cāpaṃ kārtasvaravibhūṣitam visṛjan sāyakāṃś caiva viṣāgnipratimān bahūn
english: Drawing his very great bow adorned with gold and loosing many arrows like poison and fire,
